solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Be held back by girlfriend in argument

indicators.note: the girlfriend's word holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a girlfriend is a date, someone you go out with

indicators.note: back says the word Be is to be read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round

explanation.surface: Someone is kept late by a girlfriend in the middle of a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held ... by' is split around 'back': the girlfriend holds the reversed word inside her.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is a formal argument, a discussion between opposing sides.

clue.text: Put off key publication without notice

parts.note: D is a musical key

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the publication's word goes around the notice

parts.note: an issue is an edition of a magazine or paper
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A vital publication goes out with no advance announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking' but here has its old sense 'outside', so the publication wraps around the notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissuade someone is to discourage or deter them from doing something.

clue.text: Enlarged photo for somebody

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read literally, a picture made bigger

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase read literally is a blown-up picture; as an idiom it is a person of importance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigshot is an influential person, a somebody, and taken literally a large photograph.

clue.text: Cooked trout with steamer, say — job for instructor

indicators.note: cooked suggests the fish's letters are prepared into a new form

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange
a steamer is one example of a ship, as say signals

explanation.surface: Trout prepared aboard a steamship sounds like a kitchen task, odd work for a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'job for instructor' is the post itself, not a task an instructor sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutorship is the position or post of a tutor, someone who teaches.

clue.text: Number put on uniform for one of the services

indicators.note: in this across answer the number's word is placed after, as if added on, to the other piece

parts.note: uniform means even, regular
a number is a piece of music, a song

explanation.surface: A digit is stitched onto a military uniform for a member of the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a figure but is a song; 'services' suggests the military but means church services.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer, one of the regular church services.

clue.text: It's delirium — I've distorted appearance of reality

indicators.note: distorted shows the letters of the three words are twisted into another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sufferer says delirium has warped their view of what is real.
explanation.definitionFit: Verisimilitude is the quality of seeming true or real, a semblance of truth.

clue.text: Monarch eliminated from European kingdom? Certainly not!

indicators.note: eliminated from says the monarch's letter is taken out of the kingdom's name

parts.note: Norway is a kingdom in Scandinavia
R is the abbreviation for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian state abolishing its king meets an emphatic refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: No way is an informal emphatic refusal or denial.

clue.text: Lad lost at sea turning to experienced crewman

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A boy missing on the ocean becomes a seasoned sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a veteran sailor with long seafaring experience.

clue.text: Europeans who fought the people of Paris

definitions.text: Europeans who fought the people of Paris

parts.words: Europeans who fought the people of Paris
parts.note: Paris here is the Trojan prince, not the French capital; the Trojans were fought by an ancient nation from mainland Europe

explanation.walkthrough: Paris invites thoughts of France and its citizens; it is the Trojan prince whose abduction of Helen started the Trojan War.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Trojan War the Achaeans from Hellas besieged Troy, home of Paris.

clue.text: Commander attacks all-out efforts by protesters

parts.note: a general is a senior army commander
strikes means attacks

explanation.surface: An officer launches assaults against people protesting en masse.
explanation.definitionFit: General strikes are mass walkouts across many industries, the fullest form of industrial action.

clue.text: Said to quote prophet as person having interesting views

indicators.note: said shows the word for quote is spoken, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: to cite is to quote
a seer is a prophet

explanation.surface: Someone is described as citing a prophet as a person with fascinating opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'views' suggests opinions, but a tourist looks at scenic views.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist visiting notable places spends time looking at interesting scenery.

clue.text: Golf club giving Woods, initially, slight advantage

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of Woods

parts.note: only the opening letter is used
an edge is a slight advantage

explanation.surface: Tiger Woods's club choice gives him an early small lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woods' looks like golf clubs or Tiger Woods, but only its first letter W is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge is a lofted iron used for short, high shots in golf.

clue.text: Disastrous run, so he gets put out of seat

indicators.note: disastrous signals the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rider has a calamitous outing and ends up losing his seat.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhorse is to throw a rider from the saddle.

clue.text: Boisterously frolic as high-flier

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to play about high-spiritedly
second meaning: a songbird famous for singing as it soars high

explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flier' suggests an ambitious person but is the bird that sings in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for horseplay and the name of a lark that sings while climbing.

clue.text: Discard diamonds with irritation

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
an itch is an irritation

explanation.surface: A card player throws away diamonds in annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is to get rid of or abandon it.

clue.text: Invincible military leader invading land before day's end

indicators.note: before puts the land piece ahead of the day's final letter
invading puts the leading letter inside the word for land

parts.note: to alight is to land, come down

indicators.note: leader takes the opening letter of military

parts.note: only its first letter is used

indicators.note: end picks only the final letter of the word day

parts.note: only its last letter is used

explanation.surface: An unbeatable army commander invades a country before nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes inside ALIGHT, then the last letter of 'day' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Almighty means all-powerful, so impossible to defeat.

clue.text: Evangelist's cry of support for one who's charming?

parts.note: go! is a shout of encouragement
a speller is one who casts spells, a charmer in the magical sense

explanation.surface: A preacher's cheer goes up for a charismatic person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charming' means casting spells, not being pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A gospeller is a preacher of the gospel, an evangelist.

clue.text: Pears man ruined? Hard cheese!

indicators.note: ruined says the letters are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A fruit grower loses his crop and gets an unsympathetic 'hard luck'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese!' is British slang for 'bad luck', but read literally it defines the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard Italian cheese, usually grated.

clue.text: What offers support and love to a girl?

definitions.note: noun phrase: a thing that makes an offer

parts.note: a prop is a support
love is zero in tennis, written O
Sal is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man asks what gives backing and love to a young woman, hinting at marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is a suggestion or bid put forward, notably an offer of marriage.

clue.text: About to join Conservative and another in place of minister

parts.note: re means about, concerning
another Conservative, a Tory

explanation.surface: A politician is set to join the Conservatives alongside a colleague in a government post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' suggests a government role; it is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectory is the house provided for a rector, a parish priest.

clue.text: It's found amongst Russians as handle

definitions.text: It's found amongst Russians as handle

indicators.note: found amongst says the name lies inside the run of words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A name commonly used by Russians as a nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Sasha is a familiar Russian name, a handle being slang for a name.

clue.text: Works hard to retain right in Cornish town

indicators.note: to retain means to keep within, so the town holds the letter

parts.note: St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall, south-west England

explanation.surface: Someone toils to keep their rights in a Cornish seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive is to make great efforts, to labour.

clue.text: More demanding title role in musical

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the orphan famous for asking for more gruel
second meaning: the title character of Lionel Bart's musical

explanation.walkthrough: 'More demanding' reads as a comparative adjective but means 'asking for more', the famous scene in Dickens's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist asks the workhouse master for more food, and Oliver! is the stage musical of his story.

clue.text: Light that's seen in the morning sky

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a match, an old word for a friction match
second meaning: the morning star, Venus, given its Latin name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' as a match is dated: a lucifer was an early friction match.
explanation.definitionFit: The name means light-bearer and was given to Venus rising before dawn, and to early matches.

clue.text: Morally weak female held up by bar

indicators.note: in this down answer the female's letter sits above, supported by, the bar's word

parts.note: a rail is a bar

explanation.surface: A weak-willed woman is propped up at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Frail can mean easily tempted, lacking moral strength.

clue.text: Product of mine included by those people in mathematical work

indicators.note: included by puts the mine's product inside the people's word

parts.note: them means those people
ore is what is mined

explanation.surface: A mining output is worked into some people's maths project.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a mathematical statement proved by reasoning.

clue.text: Player takes a bow for this female Shakespearean role

definitions.text: Player takes a bow for this
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stringed instrument played with a bow
second meaning: the heroine of Twelfth Night

explanation.walkthrough: 'takes a bow' suggests an actor's curtain call, but the bow is the one drawn across strings.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument is a slightly larger cousin of the violin, and the name is Twelfth Night's shipwrecked heroine.

clue.text: Child really likes receiving good gentle treatment they provide

indicators.note: receiving means the child and likes pair takes in the letter between them

parts.note: a kid is a child
loves means really likes

explanation.surface: A child loves being given good, tender care.
explanation.walkthrough: Treating someone 'with kid gloves' means handling them very gently.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft gloves of kidskin give the idiom for delicate, careful handling.

clue.text: Wrongly take solitary man with king or queen

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters are put in an incorrect order

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A lone man is mistakenly paired with royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalist is a supporter of the monarchy, someone on the side of the crown.

clue.text: Cage bird

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a place of confinement
second meaning: British slang, doing bird is serving time in jail

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cage bird' suggests a pet canary; 'bird' is British slang for a jail term, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A jail is a cage for people, and bird is slang for incarceration.
